name: Quenby Fair Share Health Cover Act

unclear.text: Whether seasonal workers count toward the 50 FTE threshold
readings: U1-a: seasonal workers count by their hours
U1-b: seasonal workers are left out of the count

a_1.text: About 135,000 full-timers at firms of 50+ FTE are offered nothing, and about 105,000 are offered less than K1 requires, so K1 binds for them.

a_2.text: Some bound firms that offer nothing now choose to offer.

a_3.text: Money wages are fixed in the short run by pay scales and yearly raises.

a_4.text: Some bound firms choose to pay the charge for at least some full-timers.

a_5.text: Some firms with plans short of K1 upgrade them rather than pay.

a_6.text: Wages above the minimum can adjust over the medium horizon, as raises are set.

a_7.text: At players, for the marginal pair, cover at 30% is worth less to the worker than its cost to the employer.

a_8.text: Workers at payers have some alternative to bound full-time work, so the wage does not fall by the whole charge.

a_9.text: The minimum wage binds for some workers at bound firms.

a_10.text: Some employers can reschedule jobs from 30 to 35 hours to under 30 at a cost below the per-head cost.

a_14.text: Some firms near 50 FTE value staying below the line more than the extra work.

a_15.text: Owners of firms near 50 know from January 2027 that the 2027 average decides 2028 status.

a_18.text: Revenue cannot cheaply verify reported offers, and some firms report offers not made.

a_21.text: Business values reflect expected earnings, and buyers expected the Act from its introduction.

a_23.text: Over the medium to long run, workers' alternatives to bound employment are clearly worse than employers' alternatives.

a_29.text: The $4.1 million is new general-fund money.

a_33.text: Some of the 380 seasonal firms do not offer qualifying cover to their full-timers.

q214_wages_paid_to_hospital_nursing_and_.text: Wages paid to hospital nursing and support staff are taxed under Quenby's 4.5% income tax.

q215_hospitals_hire_support_staff_such_a.text: Hospitals hire support staff such as aides, cleaners and kitchen workers from the same pool of low-wage workers as firms under 50 FTE.

q216_workers_at_firms_near_50_fte_spend_.text: Workers at firms near 50 FTE spend most of their earnings on present goods.

q217_some_uninsured_workers_at_firms_nea.text: Some uninsured workers at firms near 50 FTE whose earnings rise move above 200% of the poverty line.

q218_workers_at_firms_near_50_fte_who_wo.text: Workers at firms near 50 FTE who work longer hours have less time for producing goods and care at home.

q219_workers_given_longer_hours_at_firms.text: Workers given longer hours at firms near 50 FTE give up second jobs at other firms under 50 FTE.

q220_some_workers_at_firms_under_50_fte_.text: Some workers at firms under 50 FTE are paid at or near the minimum wage, so more demand for them raises hiring before it raises their wage.

q221_some_workers_at_firms_under_50_fte_.text: Some workers at firms under 50 FTE are paid enough above the minimum wage that their wage can rise with more demand for them.

q222_some_workers_living_near_marisport_.text: Some workers living near Marisport choose between jobs at Quenby firms under 50 FTE and jobs in Tarnley.

q223_some_people_who_take_added_jobs_at_.text: Some people who take added jobs at firms under 50 FTE were not in paid work before.

q224_workers_who_take_paid_jobs_have_les.text: Workers who take paid jobs have less time for producing goods and care at home.

q225_tarnley_employers_near_marisport_hi.text: Tarnley employers near Marisport hire fewer workers when the wages they must pay rise.
